claim: Recurrence prevention splits into three mechanisms that only work together: document the error finer than success/fail, reflect in retrievable language rather than weights, and evict the lesson when it is wrong. Most systems stop after step 2.
bet: Audit the workspace's own error log for which of the three mechanisms it implements; expect to find documentation and reflection present but eviction missing.

claim: The documented error can itself be the error: 0 of 121 reflections mentioned the correct target object in 16 frozen ALFWorld environments, so reflective memory can reinforce false beliefs rather than correct them.
bet: Add a provenance requirement to every stored lesson: environment-derived signal or eviction. Grounding moved correct-object mention 0% to 86% and RRR 0.64 to 0.10.

claim: Eviction is what makes insight extraction self-correcting: ExpeL downvotes an insight to zero and removes it, and states the reason — even successful trajectories can be suboptimal and mislead the generated insights.
bet: Give the project's candidate ledger a deterministic eviction trigger rather than human-only triage; RRR is the measurable precedent.

claim: Errors are a causal cascade, not a flat list: the critical error is the earliest step whose correction prevents final failure, found by counterfactual substitution — so documenting a symptom and fixing it leaves the root cause to return in a different costume.
bet: Classify each logged error by taxonomy module and mark the critical (root-cause) one; fix only those. 24.3% all-correct detection vs 0.3% baseline.
